name: meeple-no-cap-v1
description: ⭐ NO SUPPLY CAP AT ALL (Dean, 05/09/2026): "let's just remove the cap completely - there is no limit to how many or what colour meeple you can hold". This overlay is the arm that measured it before it was ruled into the defaults, and it is kept as the record of that pair. WHAT IT ASKS. The cap of one was ruled on 04/09/2026 on teach simplicity, against a sweep that preferred two; two then shipped by accident inside R17's arm; and under R17 the cap boxes only 1.14 meeples a game against 13.45 under the v1 loop, because a resource spend no longer leaves the game. So the cap had already stopped doing economic work and what was left was a rule to remember. Removing it should therefore move almost nothing, and THAT IS THE PREDICTION TO FALSIFY. ⚠️ THE ONE REAL RISK IS NOT THE BALANCE, IT IS THE BRANCHING FACTOR. Meeples pay for builds, Grows and crates, and the payment enumerator walks every subset of the supply as a count vector: at a cap of 2 that is bounded at 3^5 = 243 fills per position, and with no cap it is bounded only by how many meeples a seat has actually accumulated. A seat holding six of each colour is 7^5 = 16,807 fills, and each one multiplies the build options under it. THIS IS THE HAND-LIMIT BLOWUP'S SHAPE (02/09/2026), with meeples standing in for the extra cards. Run tools/bench-branching.ts --audit against this overlay BEFORE the suite, and read WORST LEGAL MOVES and SECONDS PER GAME first. Dean's stated tolerance for the whole balance suite is five to six minutes, and to STOP above ten. READ IN THIS ORDER. (1) Worst legal moves and seconds per game against the default. (2) The median supply held in the last third and the maximum supply reached, which is the anti-pile argument now that nothing guards it. (3) Meeples boxed per game, which under this arm can only be tolls. (4) The hook and the bonus mix, which should barely move if the prediction holds.
